description: Bounded channel close() fails to notify waiting full condition, deadlocking backpressured producer threads.
spec_notes: BoundedChannel.close must call self.not_full.notify_all() in addition to not_empty.

repo_files.channel.py:
"""Bounded producer-consumer channel."""

import threading
from typing import Any, Optional


class BoundedChannel:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int = 2):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.queue = []
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.not_empty = threading.Condition(self.lock)
        self.not_full = threading.Condition(self.lock)
        self.closed = False

    def put(self, item: Any, timeout: float = 0.5) -> bool:
        with self.lock:
            while len(self.queue) >= self.capacity and not self.closed:
                if not self.not_full.wait(timeout=timeout):
                    return False
            if self.closed:
                return False
            self.queue.append(item)
            self.not_empty.notify()
            return True

    def get(self, timeout: float = 0.5) -> Optional[Any]:
        with self.lock:
            while not self.queue and not self.closed:
                if not self.not_empty.wait(timeout=timeout):
                    return None
            if self.queue:
                item = self.queue.pop(0)
                self.not_full.notify()
                return item
            return None

    def close(self) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.closed = True
            # BUG: Only notifies not_empty condition, forgetting not_full condition,
            # deadlocking blocked producers on pipeline shutdown!
            self.not_empty.notify_all()
repo_files.pipeline.py:
"""Multi-stage processing pipeline."""

from channel import BoundedChannel
from worker import StageWorker


class ProcessingPipeline:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int = 2):
        self.in_ch = BoundedChannel(capacity=capacity)
        self.out_ch = BoundedChannel(capacity=capacity)
        self.worker = StageWorker(self.in_ch, self.out_ch, lambda x: x * 2)

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self.in_ch.close()
        self.out_ch.close()

tests.test_pipeline_deadlock.py:
import threading
import time
from channel import BoundedChannel
from pipeline import ProcessingPipeline


def test_basic_pipeline_flow():
    pipe = ProcessingPipeline(capacity=5)
    pipe.in_ch.put(10)
    pipe.in_ch.put(20)
    processed = pipe.worker.process_batch(10)
    assert processed == 2
    assert pipe.out_ch.get() == 20
    assert pipe.out_ch.get() == 40


def test_channel_close_unblocks_waiting_producers():
    ch = BoundedChannel(capacity=1)
    ch.put("item1")  # Channel is full

    blocked_flag = True
    put_success = None
    def blocked_producer():
        nonlocal blocked_flag, put_success
        put_success = ch.put("item2", timeout=5.0)
        blocked_flag = False

    t = threading.Thread(target=blocked_producer)
    t.start()
    time.sleep(0.05)
    assert blocked_flag is True

    # Closing channel must immediately unblock producer thread
    ch.close()
    t.join(timeout=0.5)
    assert blocked_flag is False
    assert put_success is False


def test_channel_close_allows_draining_remaining_items():
    ch = BoundedChannel(capacity=3)
    ch.put(1)
    ch.put(2)
    ch.close()
    assert ch.get() == 1
    assert ch.get() == 2
    assert ch.get() is None


def test_pipeline_shutdown():
    pipe = ProcessingPipeline(capacity=1)
    pipe.stop()
    assert pipe.in_ch.closed is True
    assert pipe.out_ch.closed is True
